heading: Frank de Planta
seo_description: Frank de Planta, former Royal Anglian Regiment officer and author of A Walking Tour of Italy’s WWII Battlefields, has led battlefield studies of the Italian Campaign for more than fifteen years.
lead_caption: Frank de Planta explains the progress of XIII (BR) Corps in the Liri Valley from a spot height at Point 593. Tim Ventham
lede: Frank has been fascinated by military history since childhood. He read Modern History at King’s College London, was commissioned into the Royal Anglian Regiment in 1984, and later commanded East Midlands Officers’ Training Corps in the Territorial Army.
body:
Fred Majdalany’s first-hand account of Cassino started a lifelong interest in that controversial series of battles, and from there in Anzio, which is bound up with it. He has since run battlefield studies in Spain, France and Italy.

Each year brings a new research project, often walked on the ground before it becomes part of a tour:

research.text: Researched for Wall to Wall, producers of the BBC’s *Who Do You Think You Are?*
The route of 1/6th East Surreys from the fall of Rome to the capture of Forlì
The Battle of Salerno, now a study in its own right
1st Canadian Infantry Division’s assault on the Hitler Line, 23 May 1944
128 (Hampshire) Infantry Brigade’s crossing of the Garigliano, 19 January 1944
234 Infantry Brigade’s defence of Leros, ‘Churchill’s Folly’
Eighth Army’s battle for the Gothic Line, August–September 1944
5th Canadian Armoured Division at the River Melfa, where Major John Mahony won the Victoria Cross
Writing the three-volume *A Walking Tour of Italy’s WWII Battlefields*, from Salerno to Rome
US Fifth Army’s advance to Florence and the winter of 1944–45 in the Apennines
